chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Umar ibn Adheena, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And I blew into him from My Spirit»
He said: It is a Spirit that Allah chose, selected, created, and attributed to Himself, and preferred over all other spirits. So He commanded and blew from him into Adam (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'My Spirit' in the verse 'And I blew into him from My Spirit'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the 'Spirit' blown into Adam is a distinct, created entity chosen and elevated by Allah, rather than an attribute of God Himself. This interpretation supports the Shia theological stance of *Tawhid* by distinguishing between the divine essence and the created spirit, emphasizing that the spirit was added to Adam by command, thereby affirming its status as a noble creation superior to other spirits.
